Notes on Q3 methodology: I classified an endpoint as "open" when its handler declares no `Depends(get_current_user | get_verified_user | get_admin_user | get_current_user_by_api_key)` and performs no equivalent manual check that rejects missing credentials. Two borderline cases: `GET /api/v1/chats/share/{share_id}` (`backend/open_webui/routers/chats.py:1188-1190`) uses `get_optional_verified_user` (`chats.py:65-78`), which swallows auth failures and returns `None` rather than raising — an anonymous caller reaches the handler and gets data back if the chat has a public access grant, so it's genuinely open. `GET /api/v1/retrieval/ef/{text}` (`backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py:2987-2991`) is only registered when `ENV == 'dev'`, and `ENV` defaults to `'dev'` (`backend/open_webui/env.py:133`). I excluded the SCIM data endpoints (`/Users`, `/Groups`, etc.) since they require a `get_scim_auth` bearer token (`scim.py:232-242`) — not "no authentication," just not a user login.

Q4:

A signed-in user's upload is received by `POST /api/v1/files/` (`backend/open_webui/routers/files.py:271`), guarded by `Depends(get_verified_user)` (`files.py:279`). The handler delegates to `upload_file_handler` (`files.py:315`), which reads the multipart `file`, sanitizes the filename, and calls `Storage.upload_file(file.file, filename, tags)` (`files.py:366`). With the default local storage provider, `LocalStorageProvider.upload_file` reads the raw bytes and writes them to `os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename)` on local disk (`backend/open_webui/storage/provider.py:60-67`); if a cloud provider (S3/GCS/Azure) is configured instead, the same call uploads to that backend, still staging a local copy under `UPLOAD_DIR` that gets removed afterward via `_cleanup_local_cache` (`files.py:97-108`, invoked at `files.py:268`). A `Files` row is then inserted recording the id, storage path, size, and SHA-256 hash (`files.py:399-419`).

If `process=True` (the default) and metadata references a `channel_id`, the file is linked to that channel first (`files.py:421-424`); the actual content processing runs via `process_uploaded_file` (`files.py:128`), either as a `BackgroundTasks` job (`files.py:428-436`) or inline (`files.py:439-447`). Depending on content type this transcribes audio (`transcribe`, called at `files.py:155`) or extracts/embeds document text by calling `process_file` (`backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py:1837`, invoked at `files.py:161-166` and `files.py:194-199`), which chunks and indexes the content into the vector DB; if `metadata.knowledge_id` is present and the user has write access, the file is also auto-linked into that Knowledge collection (`files.py:204-245`). Finally, `upload_file` publishes a `FILE_UPLOADED` event with the actor, file id, filename, and content type (`files.py:305-311`).
